beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:hushed, wonder]Where the Sahara is now, there was once a lake about the size of the Caspian ^Sea, the biggest lake on Earth ^today.
[d:tension][act:the question, leaning in]Then the rain ^stopped. [act:curious][tune:rise]Fast, or ^slow?

[d:calm][act:plain, explaining]From about eleven thousand to five thousand years ago, the Sahara was ^green. [act:vivid]Monsoon rains, summer rains blowing in from the ^ocean, reached deep into the ^desert@noun, and filled its ^lakes.

[d:build][go:2|0][act:curious, the method][tune:rise]^Why? [p:0.93][act:explaining, clear]A slow wobble in Earth's orbit, over thousands of years, gave northern summers a little more ^sunshine. [act:explaining, a simple picture]Warm land heats the air above it, the air rises, and wet ocean air flows in to take its ^place. [p:0.9][act:vivid]At its height, rain fell at about ten times today's ^rate.

[d:build][act:curious, the method]So how do we know when the rain ^stopped? [p:0.93][act:explaining, a simple picture]Mud and dust settle layer by layer at the bottom of lakes and ^seas, like the pages of a ^diary. [act:explaining, clear]Scientists drill out a tube of it, a sediment ^core, and read@present it page by ^page. [act:building, precise]Off the coast of ^Mauritania, the dust blown out from the land jumps about five and a half thousand years ago, within decades to ^centuries. [p:0.93][act:the counterpoint]But a lake in Chad records@verb a slow change, over thousands of ^years.

[d:build][act:grave, measured]Lake Mega-Chad shrank fast, about five thousand years ^ago. [act:the twist, wonder]Its last basin, the ^Bodélé, held water until only about a thousand years ^ago. [act:vivid]Now it's bone dry, and it is Earth's biggest source of ^dust.

[d:reveal][act:fair, weighing][tune:rise]So, was it a ^collapse? [act:clear]The best answer: sudden in some places, gradual in ^others. [act:dry, light][tune:rise]A single catastrophe that ended it ^all? [act:dry, firm][tune:fall]No evidence at ^all.
[d:build][act:curious, even]And ^people? [act:fair, even]Some argue that herders and their grazing cattle sped up the ^end. [act:the counterpoint, curious]One model says they ^slowed it.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, even][tune:rise]The Sahara switched off ^overnight? [act:the verdict, measured][tune:fall]*Mixed ^record@noun*. [act:fair]The green Sahara itself is well ^established.
[d:tension][p:0.93][act:the last word, warm][tune:fall]How fast it faded depends on where you ^stand.
